key_insight: AI-based tissue analysis found fewer mature tertiary lymphoid structures, lymph-node follicles, and plasma cells after neoadjuvant therapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma. These findings suggest differences in local and regional immune organization between treated and therapy-naive tumors.
problem_solved: The study addresses how immune structures in tumors and nearby lymph nodes differ following neoadjuvant treatment, a poorly understood aspect of the lung cancer immune environment.
method: Apply AI-based characterization to H&E whole-slide images of resected lung squamous cell carcinomas and paired proximal and distal lymph nodes.
Compare matched neoadjuvant-treated and therapy-naive groups; the supplied abstract identifies 20 treated patients.
Evaluate mature tumor-associated lymphoid structures, lymph-node follicles, and plasma cells. Detailed model and validation methods are not available in the truncated abstract.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this illustrates how computational pathology can support coordinated analysis of tumor and lymph-node immune features. The supplied text does not establish model performance, causality, or clinical predictive utility.
visual_elements: Tumor-to-lymph-node diagram showing the local and regional immune axis.
Annotated H&E image highlighting mature lymphoid structures, follicles, and plasma cells.
Treated-versus-therapy-naive comparison graphic with downward arrows for the reported reductions, without invented effect sizes.
Workflow: whole-slide images → AI-based characterization → immune-feature comparison.
paper_title: AI-based characterization of lymphoid structures and the tumor microenvironment reveals lower mature tertiary lymphoid structures, lymph-node follicles, and plasma cells after neoadjuvant therapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma
paper_authors: Arne Schmidt, Justin Nieder, Cornelius Boehm, Julika Ribbat-Idel, Marius Teodorescu
